## Motivation

This optimization targets **offline bulk processing** (batch annotation /
enrichment over a document library): a large batch of requests is fired at
a static model, **every request is fully independent** — single-turn, no
conversation history is ever reused — and **all requests carry the
identical fixed system prompt**, often thousands of tokens.

In this scenario the system prompt is the *only* content shared across
requests, which breaks the assumptions the radix cache normally relies on:

- **Full-attention models**: the shared system-prefix KV is reused, but
  every request's unique suffix is *also* inserted into the radix tree on
  finish. Since no request is ever seen twice, those suffix entries are
  pure waste — they occupy KV pages and evict useful entries until the
  batch ends.
- **Hybrid Mamba / linear-attention (SSM) models** are worse: every request
  holds a running state slot plus ping-pong tracking slots for radix
  donation, so `max_running_requests` is capped to
  `max_mamba_cache_size // 3` (ratio 3). Each finished request also donates
  its per-request suffix state into the tree, evicting the shared
  system-prefix state it just helped create.

When the deployment has a fixed system prompt, all requests can share one
chunk-aligned boundary state instead:

- warm requests hold **1 running slot** (no ping-pong, no suffix
  tracking/donation) → the mamba ratio drops from 3 to **1**, i.e. **3x
  more concurrent requests** on the same state pool;
- the per-request suffix KV and mamba state are **freed, not cached** →
  the radix tree stays tiny (exactly one shared system-prefix node), and
  suffix state never evicts the shared boundary state.

## Modifications

New flag `--system-prompt <text-or-file-path>` (inert when unset — every
patched site checks the boundary first, default behavior is
byte-identical). The system text is injected as the first chat message for
requests that carry no system role, so batch clients can omit it from
every request and save the per-request payload.

Three layers:

**Tokenizer layer** (`srt/system_prompt/`, new package):
- `SystemPrefix` renders the system block once and caches its token ids;
  each request becomes `cached_prefix_ids + ids(rest)`. A one-time
  token-identity probe verifies `prefix + ids(rest) == ids(full)` with three
  strategies (explicit bare-system render → measured length-difference →
  auto-strip for templates that inject a default system block, e.g.
  Qwen2.5-VL). On any mismatch, prefix caching silently disables itself and
  the caller falls back to a single full render — output stays
  byte-identical.
- The injected system text is padded with single-token fillers so the
  prefix length is a multiple of `mamba_cache_chunk_size()` (linear-attention
  state only checkpoints at chunk boundaries).

**Scheduler layer**:
- Warm/cold is a runtime property: the first request (empty tree) and
  post-eviction requests are cold and keep the full ping-pong + tracking
  path to (re-)capture the shared boundary state; everything after is warm
  (`is_system_prefix_warm`) and skips ping-pong allocation, suffix
  tracking, and donation.
- `Req.__init__` seeds `mamba_branching_seqlen` from the boundary;
  `init_next_round_input` re-derives it after prefix match so the seed
  survives the empty-tree first pass (otherwise the finish-time donate
  would poison the shared boundary node).
- Admission (`_mamba_gap_budget_for_req`), slot counting
  (`ensure_mamba_capacity`), alloc, lazy prealloc, and decode track masks
  all charge/filter warm requests consistently (warm = 1 slot, cold =
  `1 + mamba_initial_tracking_slots`).
- Warm requests get a sentinel ping-pong buffer pointing at reserved slot 0
  (never handed out by the allocator, filtered on free) so index consumers
  stay in bounds without a real allocation.

**Cache layer**:
- The radix tree key is truncated at the page-aligned boundary
  (`_system_kv_cap`); suffix pages are still freed → no pool leak, and the
  tree retains exactly one shared system-prefix node.
- Mamba donate length is capped at the boundary → suffix donates hit
  `mamba_exist` and are freed, never stored.
- `kv_cache_configurator`: with `--system-prompt` the mamba ratio is forced
  to 1, with a 2-slot reserve for the shared boundary state + evict/COW
  headroom.

## Accuracy Tests

- 29 CPU unit tests in `test/registered/unit/test_system_prompt.py` covering
  prompt resolution, chunk alignment, all three token-identity probe
  strategies, the warm/cold predicate, donate capping, boundary
  seeding/reseeding, and the radix key cap.
- The token-identity probe is itself the output-correctness guard: any
  template that cannot be split byte-identically disables the optimization
  and falls back to the full render, so generated tokens are unchanged by
  construction.

Measured on H100 in the offline bulk-processing scenario (independent
single-turn requests, identical fixed system prompt on every request),

## Update: production-verified fix chain added

The new commits (49e54ff289..93356ed393) are a chain of fixes for issues found when this feature ran in a production deployment (internally, on the v0.5.17-based release). They are backported onto this branch with adaptations to current main (the internal branch predates the `ReqKvInfo` migration and the removal of the `MAMBA_STATE_PER_REQ_*` constants). Summary, in causal order:

**1. Unaligned boundary crash (49e54ff289)** — the original padding-up alignment altered the token stream and a boundary that fails the identity probe at request time left the mamba pool sized for the warm steady state while every request stayed cold (over-admission crash). Now:
- The shared prefix is truncated **down** to the chunk grid instead of padded up — the full token stream stays byte-identical to the native render (the removed tail is re-prefilled per request, giving up only its cache reuse).
- A startup probe (`probe_system_prefix_or_disable`) runs **before any subprocess forks**: on probe failure the flag is cleared so pool sizing and runtime behavior stay consistent (feature-off everywhere).
- A slot-count admission budget is added for the static (non-shared) hybrid mamba pool.

**2. Phantom evictable credit (80e25e3750)** — the static-pool budget counted `mamba_evictable_size()`, but the match-time COW can only draw from the hard free list (its evict-retry can be blocked by locks on the shared boundary node). Now hard free slots only.

**3. Waiting-queue throttle (6a6f6ffacc + e29f58503d)** — the match-time mamba COW allocates the request's running slot *before* `add_one_req` can reject it, so a deep waiting queue drained the hard free list and died on free=0. The scheduler now stops pulling new requests once the remaining slot budget can't cover a worst-case cold request (`_mamba_match_headroom`).

**4. Audit logs (a08d87f9e0 + 092a49ec50)** — periodic `[MambaAudit]` lines reconcile the physical pool state against logical holders; made slot leaks and the crash root cause observable.

**5. Budget blind to match-time COW (1bf88bde57)** — the slot budget keyed on `mamba_pool_idx is None`, but the match COW sets that field *before* the budget runs, so every queued request was charged zero while its COW drained the free list. Fixed by sampling `fresh_cow` pre-match. Also: the warm sentinel ping-pong buffer is guarded against decode post-processing (it would otherwise free reserved slot 0 into the allocator), the token-concat fast path only engages when the leading system message content equals the fixed prompt (a client-supplied different system must not be silently replaced), and a per-request render failure now falls back to the full render instead of raising.

Unit tests grew from 29 to 44 cases covering the truncate-down invariants, the startup probe gate, the static-pool budget, the match headroom, and the fresh_cow accounting.

+"""Seeding the mamba tracking boundary for the fixed system prompt.
+
+For hybrid SSM (linear-attention) models the radix cache only reuses state at
+checkpoints aligned to ``mamba_cache_chunk_size``. Reusing the existing
+``req.mamba_branching_seqlen`` mechanism (already used at prefix-match branch
+points, see schedule_batch.py handling of it) lets us stop mamba tracking right
+after the fixed system prefix. The prefix token count is padded to a chunk
+boundary on the tokenizer side, so the boundary here is already aligned when set.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from typing import Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def cap_mamba_donate_len(
+    cache_len: Optional[int],
+    boundary: Optional[int],
+    extra_buffer: bool,
+) -> Optional[int]:
+    """Cap a mamba donate length at the fixed system-prefix ``boundary``.
+
+    With ``--system-prompt`` the tree should retain ONLY the shared system-prefix
+    mamba state and free every per-request suffix state. Capping the donate
+    length at the (chunk-aligned) boundary makes every request map to the same
+    shared boundary node; suffix donates then hit ``mamba_exist`` and the donated
+    state is freed, never stored. The boundary state itself is captured during
+    prefill by ``mamba_branching_seqlen`` (see :func:`seed_mamba_boundary`).
+
+    extra_buffer only: the ping-pong donate yields the tracked boundary state, so
+    capping the key to the boundary is consistent. ``no_buffer`` donates the live
+    chunk-end state (it ignores ``mamba_last_track_seqlen``), so capping there
+    would store a WRONG state at the boundary node -> we return ``cache_len``
+    unchanged and keep default behavior. Returns ``cache_len`` unchanged whenever
+    the feature is off (``boundary`` unset) or ``cache_len`` is None.
+    """
+    if boundary is None or boundary <= 0 or cache_len is None or not extra_buffer:
+        return cache_len
+    return min(cache_len, boundary)
+
+
+def is_system_prefix_warm(
+    boundary: Optional[int],
+    prefix_indices_len: int,
+    mamba_branching_seqlen: Optional[int],
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether a request reuses an already-cached fixed system-prefix state.
+
+    A request is "warm" when the shared system-prefix boundary is fully covered
+    by the matched prefix (``prefix_indices_len >= boundary``) AND the mamba
+    boundary state already lives in the tree (``mamba_branching_seqlen is None``
+    — the match found no branching point to re-track). Such a request only runs
+    its suffix, donates nothing (``cap_mamba_donate_len`` caps at the boundary),
+    and therefore needs no ping-pong tracking slot. Cold requests (first warm-up
+    pass, or mamba state evicted) keep the full ping-pong + tracking path so the
+    shared boundary state can be (re-)captured and donated.
+
+    Takes primitives rather than ``Req`` to stay free of import cycles; callers
+    pass ``req.system_prefix_boundary``, ``req.prefix_len`` and
+    ``req.mamba_branching_seqlen``.
+    """
+    return (
+        boundary is not None
+        and boundary > 0
+        and prefix_indices_len >= boundary
+        and mamba_branching_seqlen is None
+    )
+

+def seed_mamba_boundary(boundary_len: Optional[int], chunk: int) -> Optional[int]:
+    """Return the boundary aligned for mamba tracking, or None to keep default.
+
+    ``boundary_len`` is the fixed system-prefix length in tokens (already
+    truncated down to a chunk multiple by ``SystemPrefix._truncate_boundary``),
+    so the misaligned branch below is a last line of defense that should be
+    unreachable. We return the length unchanged if it is a positive multiple of
+    ``chunk``; anything else returns None so the runtime keeps its default (no
+    system-prompt mamba limiting) — but loudly, because a misaligned boundary
+    still flows into the other layers (KV cap, donate cap, pool ratio), which
+    is exactly the half-enabled state the startup probe exists to prevent.

+The fixed system prompt is shared by every chat request. When `--system-prompt`
+is set the value is either the literal prompt text or a path to a UTF-8 file

+for None before calling anything else, so the default code paths stay
+byte-identical.

+import os
+from typing import Optional

+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

+def resolve_system_prompt(server_args) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Return the fixed system-prompt text, or None if the feature is disabled.
+
+    The literal value is used as-is unless it names an existing file, in which
+    case the file is read as UTF-8 (trailing whitespace stripped). Long content
+    (large files) is fully supported because we only hold the text in memory.
+    """
+    value = getattr(server_args, "system_prompt", None)
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    if os.path.isfile(value):
+        try:
+            with open(value, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+                return f.read().rstrip()
+        except OSError as e:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"--system-prompt file '{value}' could not be read: {e}"
+            ) from e
+    return value
+
+
+def aligned_prefix_len_down(prefix_len: int, chunk: int) -> int:
+    """Round a raw prefix token count down to the previous ``chunk`` boundary.
+
+    Linear-attention (SSM / Mamba) state only checkpoints at multiples of
+    ``mamba_cache_chunk_size``, so the shared prefix must end exactly on a
+    chunk multiple for its state to be reusable. Truncating DOWN (instead of
+    padding up) keeps every request's full token stream identical to the
+    native render — the removed tail tokens simply stay part of each
+    request's private prefill, giving up only their cache reuse.
+    """
+    if chunk <= 0:
+        return prefix_len
+    return (prefix_len // chunk) * chunk

+    kv_cache_configurator, which forces ratio 1 whenever
+    ``server_args.system_prompt`` is set — keys off the flag alone. But the
+    feature is only actually live when the tokenizer-side probe succeeds AND
+    the system block spans at least one mamba chunk (truncate-down). If the
+    probe only failed later at request time, the pool would already be sized
+    for the warm steady state (1 slot per request) while every request stays
+    cold (3 slots each) — the over-admission crash this gate prevents.

+    failure clear ``server_args.system_prompt`` so every consumer sees a

+"""Tokens for a FIXED system prompt: inject once + cache the system prefix.
+
+The system prompt is rendered by the chat template once and its token ids
+cached. Each chat request then becomes ``cached_system_ids + ids(rest)`` so the
+shared system block is neither re-rendered nor re-tokenized per request.
+
+Correctness is guaranteed by a one-time probe: we compare
+``render(system) + render(rest)`` against a single ``render(full)`` for the same
+messages. Jinja chat templates are per-message, so the split normally reproduces
+the full token stream exactly; templates that emit context outside the
+per-message loop (a leading BOS token) are handled by stripping the duplicated
+leading BOS from the ``rest`` render. If the probe ever disagrees, prefix
+caching is disabled and the caller falls back to a single full render, so output
+remains byte-identical.
+
+Cache sharing is bounded by the mamba checkpoint grid: linear-attention state
+only exists at multiples of ``mamba_cache_chunk_size``, so the shared prefix is
+truncated DOWN to the previous chunk boundary (see ``SystemPrefix.prepare``).
+The removed tail tokens stay part of every request's private prefill, so the
+model still sees the exact native token stream (byte-identical output) — only
+the tail's cache reuse (typically < one chunk, 2-3% of a long system prompt) is
+given up. A system block shorter than one chunk disables the feature: there is
+no reusable boundary to share.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from typing import Dict, List, Optional
+
+from sglang.srt.system_prompt.system_prompt import aligned_prefix_len_down
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class SystemPrefix:
+    """Cached token prefix for a fixed system prompt."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tokenizer, system_text: str) -> None:
+        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
+        self.system_text = system_text
+        self._system_msg = {"role": "system", "content": system_text}
+        # Shared prefix, truncated to a chunk boundary; None when disabled.
+        self._prefix_ids: Optional[List[int]] = None
+        # Tail of the system block past the boundary — re-prefilled per request
+        # (private, never donated to the radix tree). Empty when the system
+        # block lands exactly on a boundary.
+        self._suffix_ids: List[int] = []
+        self._encode_kwargs: dict = {}
+        self._enabled: bool = False
+        self._boundary_len: int = 0
+        # When a chat template auto-injects a default system message into any
+        # render whose list does not start with a `system` role (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL
+        # -> "You are a helpful assistant."), we cache that auto-block and strip
+        # it from the per-request `render([rest])` before appending the cached
+        # real system prefix. None when not needed.
+        self._auto_prefix: Optional[List[int]] = None
+
+    # -- public ---------------------------------------------------------
+    @property
+    def enabled(self) -> bool:
+        return self._enabled
+
+    @property
+    def prefix_ids(self) -> Optional[List[int]]:
+        return self._prefix_ids
+
+    @property
+    def prefix_len(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._prefix_ids) if self._prefix_ids is not None else 0
+
+    @property
+    def boundary_len(self) -> int:
+        """System-prefix length in tokens, aligned DOWN to the cache chunk grid.
+
+        This is the position the scheduler truncates radix KV / mamba state at,
+        so it is valid regardless of whether the request is multimodal (the
+        system block is text-only and sits before any media). 0 when disabled.
+        """
+        return self._boundary_len
+
+    @property
+    def suffix_len(self) -> int:
+        """Per-request tail length: system-block tokens past the boundary."""
+        return len(self._suffix_ids)
+
+    def inject_message(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
+        """The message to inject so the real prompt contains the system prefix.
+
+        The ORIGINAL system text is injected: with truncate-down the shared
+        prefix is a prefix of the native render, so no padding is ever added
+        and every request's full token stream stays byte-identical.
+        """
+        return {"role": "system", "content": self.system_text}
+
+    def prepare(self, chunk: int, encode_kwargs: dict) -> None:
+        """Run the token-identity probe once and cache the system prefix.
+
+        Three probe paths, selected by template capability; the first whose
+        token-identity check ``prefix + ids(rest) == full`` passes wins:
+        * Explicit: the template can render a bare system message (handles
+          top-BOS templates correctly).
+        * Measured: the template rejects a system-only render (e.g. Qwen 3.5/3.6)
+          -> system-block length = ``len([system,user]) - len([user])``.
+        * Auto-strip: the template injects a default system block into any
+          render not starting with `system` (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL), so the split is
+          recovered via a longest-common-suffix match.
+        The recovered FULL system block is then truncated down to a chunk
+        boundary. On any failure caching stays disabled (callers fall back to
+        the full render), so output remains byte-identical.
+        """
+        self._encode_kwargs = encode_kwargs
+        self._enabled = False
+        self._prefix_ids = None
+        self._suffix_ids = []
+        self._boundary_len = 0
+        path = (
+            _prepare_explicit(self, chunk, encode_kwargs)
+            or _prepare_measured(self, chunk, encode_kwargs)
+            or _prepare_auto_strip(self, chunk, encode_kwargs)
+        )
+        if path is None:
+            logger.info("SystemPrompt prefix caching disabled by identity probe")
+            return
+        if self._truncate_boundary(chunk):
+            logger.info(
+                "SystemPrompt prefix caching enabled (%s): shared prefix=%d "
+                "tokens, per-request tail=%d tokens (chunk=%d)",
+                path,
+                self._boundary_len,
+                len(self._suffix_ids),
+                chunk,
+            )
+
+    # -- request-time ---------------------------------------------------
+    def split_request(
+        self, messages_after_system: List[Dict[str, str]], encode_kwargs: dict
+    ) -> Optional[List[int]]:
+        """Return ``prefix + ids(rest)`` for a chat, or None to use the full path.
+
+        ``messages_after_system`` is the message list with the system message as
+        the first element. Returns None when prefix caching is disabled or only
+        a system message is present (nothing to concatenate). The result starts
+        with the shared boundary-aligned prefix followed by the per-request
+        tail (system-block remainder) — together the full native token stream.
+        """
+        if not self._enabled or len(messages_after_system) < 2:
+            return None
+        self._encode_kwargs = encode_kwargs
+        rest = self._render(
+            messages_after_system[1:], add_generation_prompt=True, encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs
+        )
+        if rest is None:
+            # The per-request render failed (e.g. a template that rejects this
+            # message shape). Fall back to the caller's full-render path.
+            return None
+        if self._auto_prefix:
+            # Strip the template's auto-injected default system block from the
+            # head of the user render so `cached_sys + rest` matches a full render.
+            ap = len(self._auto_prefix)
+            if len(rest) >= ap and rest[:ap] == self._auto_prefix:
+                rest = rest[ap:]
+        rest = self._strip_leading_bos(rest)
+        return list(self._prefix_ids) + list(self._suffix_ids) + rest
+
+    # -- internal -------------------------------------------------------
+    def _truncate_boundary(self, chunk: int) -> bool:
+        """Truncate the shared prefix down to a chunk boundary. False = disable.
+
+        Called once by ``prepare`` after a probe path succeeded with the FULL
+        system block in ``_prefix_ids``. Splits it into the shared chunk-aligned
+        prefix and a per-request tail. A block shorter than one chunk leaves
+        nothing shareable: boundary 0 would make every request cold while the
+        mamba pool is planned for the warm steady state — the exact
+        over-admission crash this guard prevents — so the feature is disabled.
+        """
+        full = self._prefix_ids
+        boundary = aligned_prefix_len_down(len(full), chunk)
+        if boundary <= 0:
+            logger.warning(
+                "SystemPrompt prefix (%d tokens) is shorter than one mamba "
+                "chunk (%d): no reusable boundary, prefix caching disabled",
+                len(full),
+                chunk,
+            )
+            self._prefix_ids = None
+            self._boundary_len = 0
+            return False
+        self._suffix_ids = list(full[boundary:])
+        self._prefix_ids = list(full[:boundary])
+        self._boundary_len = boundary
+        self._enabled = True
+        assert self._boundary_len % chunk == 0
+        return True
+
+    def _render(self, msgs, add_generation_prompt: bool, encode_kwargs: dict) -> Optional[List[int]]:
+        try:
+            rendered = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+                msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=add_generation_prompt
+            )
+            return self.tokenizer.encode(rendered, **encode_kwargs)
+        except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
+            logger.warning("SystemPrompt render failed: %s", e)
+            return None
+
+    def _strip_leading_bos(self, token_ids: List[int]) -> List[int]:
+        return _strip_leading_bos(token_ids, getattr(self.tokenizer, "bos_token_id", None))
+
+
+def _strip_leading_bos(token_ids: List[int], bos_id: Optional[int]) -> List[int]:
+    if bos_id is None or not token_ids or token_ids[0] != bos_id:
+        return token_ids
+    return token_ids[1:]
+
+
+def _prepare_explicit(seam, chunk: int, encode_kwargs: dict) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Probe for templates that can render a bare system message."""
+    sample_user = {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}
+    try:
+        sys_ids = seam._render(
+            [seam._system_msg], add_generation_prompt=False, encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs
+        )
+        if sys_ids is None:
+            return None
+        user_ids = seam._render(
+            [sample_user], add_generation_prompt=True, encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs
+        )
+        full_ids = seam._render(
+            [seam._system_msg, sample_user],
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs,
+        )

+            return None
+        rest = _strip_leading_bos(user_ids, getattr(seam.tokenizer, "bos_token_id", None))
+        if sys_ids + rest != full_ids:
+            return None
+        seam._prefix_ids = list(sys_ids)
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+    return "explicit"
+
+
+def _prepare_measured(seam, chunk: int, encode_kwargs: dict) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Fallback for templates that require a user turn to render (e.g. Qwen3.x)."""
+    sample_user = {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}
+    try:
+        user_ids = seam._render(
+            [sample_user], add_generation_prompt=True, encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs
+        )
+        full_ids = seam._render(
+            [seam._system_msg, sample_user],
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs,
+        )
+        if full_ids is None or user_ids is None:
+            return None
+        sys_len = len(full_ids) - len(user_ids)
+        if sys_len <= 0:
+            return None
+        prefix = list(full_ids[:sys_len])
+        rest = _strip_leading_bos(user_ids, getattr(seam.tokenizer, "bos_token_id", None))
+        if prefix + rest != full_ids:
+            return None
+        seam._prefix_ids = prefix
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+    return "measured"
+
+
+def _prepare_auto_strip(seam, chunk: int, encode_kwargs: dict) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Last resort for templates that auto-insert a default system message.
+
+    When a template injects a default `system` block into any render whose
+    message list does not start with a `system` role (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL inserts
+    "You are a helpful assistant."), rendering the user part alone differs from
+    the full conversation by exactly that fixed leading block. We detect it via
+    the longest common SUFFIX of the user-only render and the full render (the
+    shared user block), recovering both the real system prefix (the full render
+    minus that suffix) and the auto-block (the user render minus that suffix).
+    ``split_request`` then strips the auto-block so that
+    ``cached_real_system + rest == full``.
+    """
+    sample_user = {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}
+    try:
+        user_ids = seam._render(
+            [sample_user], add_generation_prompt=True, encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs
+        )
+        full_ids = seam._render(
+            [seam._system_msg, sample_user],
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs,
+        )
+        if user_ids is None or full_ids is None:
+            return None
+        n = min(len(full_ids), len(user_ids))
+        i = 0
+        while i < n and full_ids[-1 - i] == user_ids[-1 - i]:
+            i += 1
+        if i == 0:
+            return None
+        shared_tail = i
+        sys_prefix = list(full_ids[: len(full_ids) - shared_tail])
+        auto_prefix = list(user_ids[: len(user_ids) - shared_tail])
+        if not sys_prefix or not auto_prefix:
+            return None

+        # specific user content, otherwise user tokens leaked into it.
+        sample2 = {"role": "user", "content": "hello world!"}
+        full2 = seam._render(
+            [seam._system_msg, sample2],
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs,
+        )
+        user2 = seam._render(
+            [sample2], add_generation_prompt=True, encode_kwargs=encode_kwargs
+        )

+            k = min(len(full2), len(user2))
+            j = 0
+            while j < k and full2[-1 - j] == user2[-1 - j]:
+                j += 1
+            sys2 = list(full2[: len(full2) - j])
+            if sys2 != sys_prefix:
+                return None
+
+        seam._auto_prefix = auto_prefix
+        seam._prefix_ids = sys_prefix
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+    return "auto-strip"

+        self._id = {c: i + 20 for i, c in enumerate("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")}
+        for d in "0123456789":

+        if self._require_user and not any(m["role"] == "user" for m in messages):
+            raise ValueError("No user query found in messages.")
+        if self._noisy:
+            self._noise += 1
+            out = f"<{self._noise}N>"

+        if self._top_bos:

+class TestReseedAfterMatch(CustomTestCase):
+    """The post-match re-derivation that keeps the boundary seed alive.
+
+    Bug regression: ``init_next_round_input`` overwrote
+    ``mamba_branching_seqlen`` with the match result unconditionally, so on an
+    empty tree (first warm-up request) the ``__init__``-seeded boundary died and
+    prefill tracked the prompt tail instead of the boundary; the finish donate
+    then stored the tail state under the boundary-capped key, poisoning the
+    shared node for every later warm request. Each case below guards one
+    branch of the re-derivation.
+    """
+
+    def test_first_request_restores_seed(self):
+        # Empty tree: match returns prefix 0 and branching None -> the seed
+        # must come back so prefill tracks the boundary state.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            reseed_mamba_boundary_after_match(64, 0, None),
+            64,
+        )
+
+    def test_cold_partial_prefix_restores_seed(self):
+        # KV partially cached but boundary not covered, no branching point ->
+        # still the warm-up pass; track the boundary.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            reseed_mamba_boundary_after_match(64, 32, None),
+            64,
+        )
+
+    def test_match_branching_wins(self):
+        # Mamba state evicted (match found a branching point to re-track):
+        # the match's recovery plan must not be clobbered by the seed.
+        self.assertEqual(
+            reseed_mamba_boundary_after_match(64, 32, 32),
+            32,
+        )
+
+    def test_warm_stays_none(self):
+        # Boundary fully covered, no branching point: warm request. Returning
+        # the seed here would flip is_system_prefix_warm to False and cost the
+        # request a full ping-pong path (concurrency regression to pool/3).
+        self.assertIsNone(reseed_mamba_boundary_after_match(64, 64, None))
+        self.assertIsNone(reseed_mamba_boundary_after_match(64, 100, None))
+
+    def test_feature_off_passthrough(self):
+        # Default path stays byte-identical: without a boundary the match
+        # result passes through untouched, warm or not.
+        self.assertIsNone(reseed_mamba_boundary_after_match(None, 0, None))
+        self.assertEqual(reseed_mamba_boundary_after_match(None, 0, 32), 32)
+

+class TestSystemPrefixWarm(CustomTestCase):
+    """The warm/cold predicate driving the mamba slot-factor optimization.
+
+    A request is warm only when the shared system-prefix boundary is fully
+    covered by the matched prefix AND the mamba boundary state already lives in
+    the tree (match left no branching point). Each cold branch below guards a
+    distinct failure mode: if the predicate flipped to always-True, cold
+    requests (warm-up / post-eviction) would skip tracking, never (re-)donate
+    the boundary state, and every subsequent request would run from a stale /
+    zero mamba state; if it flipped to always-False, the slot-factor savings
+    vanish and concurrency regresses to pool/3.
+    """
+
+    def test_warm_when_boundary_cached(self):
+        self.assertTrue(is_system_prefix_warm(64, 64, None))
+        self.assertTrue(is_system_prefix_warm(64, 100, None))
+
+    def test_cold_when_boundary_unset(self):
+        # Feature off / client-supplied system message: no boundary -> never
+        # warm (default path unchanged).
+        self.assertFalse(is_system_prefix_warm(None, 100, None))
+        self.assertFalse(is_system_prefix_warm(0, 100, None))
+
+    def test_cold_first_request_prefix_short(self):
+        # Warm-up pass: tree empty, matched prefix shorter than the boundary
+        # -> must be cold so it tracks and donates the shared boundary state.
+        self.assertFalse(is_system_prefix_warm(64, 0, None))
+        self.assertFalse(is_system_prefix_warm(64, 32, None))
+
+    def test_cold_after_mamba_eviction(self):
+        # KV prefix still covers the boundary but the mamba state was evicted,
+        # so the match returned a branching point (non-None) to re-track ->
+        # must be cold so the boundary state is re-captured, not skipped.
+        self.assertFalse(is_system_prefix_warm(64, 100, 64))
+

+class TestMambaDonateCap(CustomTestCase):
+    """The cap that makes the tree retain only the shared system-prefix state.
+
+    Each case guards a distinct failure mode of ``cap_mamba_donate_len``: the
+    cap fires only in extra_buffer mode and only when the boundary is set, else
+    the donate length passes through unchanged. no_buffer must NOT be capped
+    (its donate is the live chunk-end state, not the boundary state, so capping
+    would store a wrong state at the shared boundary node).
+    """
+
+    def test_caps_suffix_donate_in_extra_buffer(self):
+        # Guards the core fix: a suffix donate (cache_len 200 > boundary 64)
+        # must be capped to the boundary so it maps to the shared node and the
+        # suffix state is freed via mamba_exist. Removing the min -> per-request
+        # suffix states leak into the tree (the bug being fixed).
+        self.assertEqual(cap_mamba_donate_len(200, 64, True), 64)
+
+    def test_no_cap_in_no_buffer(self):
+        # Guards the safety gate: no_buffer donates the live chunk-end state, so
+        # capping its key to the boundary would store a WRONG state at the shared
+        # boundary node (silent output corruption). Removing the extra_buffer
+        # guard -> this turns red and the corruption path reopens.
+        self.assertEqual(cap_mamba_donate_len(200, 64, False), 200)
+
+    def test_passthrough_when_feature_off(self):
+        # Default path stays byte-identical: with no boundary the donate length
+        # is unchanged in both modes. Removing the boundary-None check -> red.
+        self.assertEqual(cap_mamba_donate_len(200, None, True), 200)
+        self.assertEqual(cap_mamba_donate_len(200, None, False), 200)
+
+    def test_none_cache_len_passthrough(self):
+        # mamba_last_track_seqlen is None mid-decode / before any track; the cap
+        # must not crash on it. Removing the cache_len-None guard -> TypeError.
+        self.assertIsNone(cap_mamba_donate_len(None, 64, True))
+
+
+class TestSystemPrefix(CustomTestCase):
+    def _render(self, tok, msgs, gen):
+        return tok.encode(tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=gen))
+
+    def _run(self, top_bos, chunk):
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=top_bos)
+        sp = SystemPrefix(tok, "SYS")
+        sp.prepare(chunk, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertTrue(sp.enabled, "identity probe should enable caching")
+        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": "SYS"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}]
+        got = sp.split_request(msgs, encode_kwargs={})
+        full = self._render(tok, msgs, gen=True)
+        real_sys = self._render(tok, msgs[:1], gen=False)
+        # truncate-down invariants (see TestTruncateDownInvariants)
+        self.assertEqual(got, full)
+        self.assertEqual(sp.prefix_len, (len(real_sys) // chunk) * chunk)
+        self.assertEqual(sp.prefix_len % chunk, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(got[: sp.prefix_len], list(sp.prefix_ids))
+        # inject_message carries the ORIGINAL text: no padding ever added
+        self.assertEqual(sp.inject_message()["content"], "SYS")
+
+    def test_split_qwen_style(self):
+        for chunk in (3, 4):
+            with self.subTest(chunk=chunk):
+                self._run(top_bos=False, chunk=chunk)
+
+    def test_split_llama_style_top_bos(self):
+        for chunk in (3, 4):
+            with self.subTest(chunk=chunk):
+                self._run(top_bos=True, chunk=chunk)
+
+    def test_split_disabled_on_identity_mismatch(self):
+        # Non-deterministic template: each render gets a fresh leading token, so
+        # no stable system prefix can be cached -> caching must be disabled and
+        # split_request must return None (fall back to the full render).
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False, noisy=True)
+        sp = SystemPrefix(tok, "SYS")
+        sp.prepare(3, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertFalse(sp.enabled)
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            sp.split_request(
+                [{"role": "system", "content": "SYS"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}],
+                encode_kwargs={},
+            )
+        )
+
+    def test_measured_path_user_required(self):
+        # Qwen-style template rejects a bare system render; the measured path
+        # must still produce an aligned prefix and a split that reproduces the
+        # native full render (inject_message = original text).
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False, require_user=True)
+        sp = SystemPrefix(tok, "SYS")
+        sp.prepare(4, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertTrue(sp.enabled)
+        self.assertTrue(sp.prefix_len % 4 == 0)
+        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": "SYS"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}]
+        full = self._render(tok, msgs, gen=True)
+        got = sp.split_request(msgs, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertEqual(got, full)
+
+    def test_prefix_len_matches_boundary(self):
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False)
+        sp = SystemPrefix(tok, "SYS")
+        sp.prepare(12, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertEqual(seed_mamba_boundary(sp.prefix_len, 12), sp.prefix_len)
+        self.assertEqual(sp.prefix_len % 12, 0)
+
+    def test_auto_strip_default_system(self):
+        # Qwen2.5-VL-style template: rendering user alone auto-prepends a default
+        # system block. auto-strip must recover it and reconstruct the native
+        # `full` render exactly (no padding — the Qwen3.8-27B crash regression:
+        # auto-strip used to skip chunk alignment entirely).
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False, require_user=True, stateful=True)
+        sp = SystemPrefix(tok, "SYS")
+        sp.prepare(4, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertTrue(sp.enabled)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(sp._auto_prefix)
+        self.assertEqual(sp.prefix_len % 4, 0)
+        msgs = [sp.inject_message(), {"role": "user", "content": "U"}]
+        full = self._render(tok, msgs, gen=True)
+        got = sp.split_request(msgs, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertIsNotNone(got)
+        self.assertEqual(got, full)
+
+
+class TestTruncateDownInvariants(CustomTestCase):
+    """Derived property: truncate-down never changes the token stream.
+
+    For every chunk size, the shared prefix must be the native system block
+    truncated DOWN to the grid, and prefix + tail + rest must reproduce the
+    native full render token-for-token. A regression to pad-up (or to an
+    off-grid boundary) turns these red: pad-up changes `got` (extra pad tokens
+    not in `full`), an off-grid boundary breaks the `% chunk` check and would
+    put the boundary between mamba checkpoints — the half-enabled crash state.
+    """
+
+    SYS_TEXT = "S" * 40  # "<|system|>" + 40 chars -> 50 tokens with this stub
+
+    def test_boundary_is_floor_and_stream_is_native(self):
+        for chunk in (5, 8, 16, 30, 64):
+            with self.subTest(chunk=chunk):
+                tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False)
+                sp = SystemPrefix(tok, self.SYS_TEXT)
+                sp.prepare(chunk, encode_kwargs={})
+                real_sys = tok.encode(
+                    tok.apply_chat_template(
+                        [{"role": "system", "content": self.SYS_TEXT}],
+                        tokenize=False,
+                        add_generation_prompt=False,
+                    )
+                )
+                if len(real_sys) < chunk:
+                    # covered by TestShortSystemDisables; here every chunk fits
+                    self.assertFalse(sp.enabled)
+                    continue
+                self.assertTrue(sp.enabled)
+                self.assertEqual(sp.boundary_len, (len(real_sys) // chunk) * chunk)
+                self.assertEqual(sp.prefix_len, sp.boundary_len)
+                self.assertEqual(sp.suffix_len, len(real_sys) - sp.boundary_len)
+                msgs = [
+                    {"role": "system", "content": self.SYS_TEXT},
+                    {"role": "user", "content": "U"},
+                ]
+                full = tok.encode(
+                    tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
+                )
+                got = sp.split_request(msgs, encode_kwargs={})
+                self.assertEqual(got, full)
+                self.assertEqual(got[: sp.boundary_len], list(sp.prefix_ids))
+
+
+class TestShortSystemDisables(CustomTestCase):
+    """Bug regression (Qwen3.8-27B crash): a system block shorter than one
+    mamba chunk used to flow through with an unusable boundary — every request
+    stayed cold (3 slots) while the pool was sized for warm (1 slot/req) and
+    the first batch crashed the mamba allocator. A block that leaves no
+    chunk-aligned boundary must disable the feature entirely.
+    """
+
+    def test_short_system_disables(self):
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False)
+        sp = SystemPrefix(tok, "SYS")  # 13 tokens with this stub
+        sp.prepare(30, encode_kwargs={})
+        self.assertFalse(sp.enabled)
+        self.assertEqual(sp.boundary_len, 0)
+        self.assertIsNone(sp.prefix_ids)
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            sp.split_request(
+                [{"role": "system", "content": "SYS"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}],
+                encode_kwargs={},
+            )
+        )
+
+
+class TestStartupProbeGate(CustomTestCase):
+    """Bug regression (Qwen3.8-27B crash): the mamba pool sized itself for the
+    warm steady state (ratio 1) purely from ``server_args.system_prompt`` being
+    set, before any probe ran. When the runtime probe later failed, every
+    request was cold on a warm-sized pool -> over-admission crash. The startup
+    gate must clear the flag (end-to-end feature-off) whenever the probe fails.
+    """
+
+    def _args(self, chunk=16):
+        return _FakeArgs(
+            "SYS-TEXT", model_path="/tmp/m", mamba_cache_chunk_size=chunk
+        )
+
+    def test_probe_ok_keeps_flag(self):
+        args = self._args(chunk=8)
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False)
+        with patch(
+            "transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained", return_value=tok
+        ):
+            probe_system_prefix_or_disable(args)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(args.system_prompt)
+
+    def test_probe_reject_short_system_clears_flag(self):
+        # chunk 64 > the stub's 13-token system block: probe disables -> the
+        # gate must clear server_args.system_prompt before schedulers fork.
+        args = self._args(chunk=64)
+        tok = _StubTokenizer(top_bos=False)
+        with patch(
+            "transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained", return_value=tok
+        ):
+            probe_system_prefix_or_disable(args)
+        self.assertIsNone(args.system_prompt)
+
+    def test_tokenizer_load_failure_clears_flag(self):
+        # A probe that cannot even load the tokenizer must fall back to the
+        # native path rather than risk the half-enabled state.
+        args = self._args()
+        with patch(
+            "transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained",
+            side_effect=RuntimeError("boom"),
+        ):
+            probe_system_prefix_or_disable(args)
+        self.assertIsNone(args.system_prompt)
+
+    def test_unset_flag_is_noop(self):
+        args = _FakeArgs(None)
+        probe_system_prefix_or_disable(args)
+        self.assertIsNone(args.system_prompt)
+
+
+class TestStaticMambaSlotBudget(CustomTestCase):
+    """Bug regression (Qwen3.8-27B crash): on the static (non-shared) hybrid
+    mamba pool the PrefillAdder charged nothing per request, so a cold burst
+    (each req taking running + ping-pong = 3 slots) over-admitted past the
+    ratio-1-sized pool and died in the fail-loud allocator. The slot budget
+    must charge cold requests the full factor and warm requests 1.
+    """
+
+    def _adder(self, static: bool, lazy: bool = False):
+        adder = SimpleNamespace(
+            _static_mamba_slots=static,
+            tree_cache=SimpleNamespace(
+                req_to_token_pool=SimpleNamespace(
+                    # main's pool exposes the initial tracking slots directly
+                    # (2 with overlap, 1 in lazy mode) instead of the lazy flag.
+                    mamba_initial_tracking_slots=1 if lazy else 2
+                )
+            ),
+        )
+        return adder
+
+    def _req(self, boundary, prefix_len=0, branching=None, has_pool_idx=False):
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            system_prefix_boundary=boundary,
+            prefix_len=prefix_len,
+            mamba_branching_seqlen=branching,
+            kv=SimpleNamespace(
+                mamba_pool_idx=0 if has_pool_idx else None
+            ),
+        )
+
+    def _budget(self, adder, req, fresh_cow=False):
+        from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_policy import PrefillAdder
+
+        return PrefillAdder._mamba_slot_budget_for_req(adder, req, fresh_cow=fresh_cow)
+
+    def test_cold_charged_full_factor(self):
+        # Warm-up burst: no boundary coverage -> 3 slots (running+ping-pong).
+        adder = self._adder(static=True)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 0, None)), 3)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 32, None)), 3)
+
+    def test_warm_charged_one(self):
+        # Steady state: boundary covered, no branching -> sentinel-only
+        # ping-pong, 1 slot.
+        adder = self._adder(static=True)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 64, None)), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 100, None)), 1)
+
+    def test_cold_after_eviction(self):
+        # Branching point from the match (mamba state evicted) -> cold again.
+        adder = self._adder(static=True)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 100, 64)), 3)
+
+    def test_lazy_pool_charges_two(self):
+        adder = self._adder(static=True, lazy=True)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 0, None)), 2)
+
+    def test_zero_when_not_static(self):
+        # Shared pool / non-mamba: slot budgeting happens via the token
+        # reserve; charging here too would double-count.
+        adder = self._adder(static=False)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 0, None)), 0)
+
+    def test_zero_when_pool_idx_held(self):
+        # Re-added request that already holds its mamba slot: alloc will not
+        # re-allocate, so admission must not charge again.
+        adder = self._adder(static=True)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 0, None, has_pool_idx=True)), 0)
+
+    def test_fresh_cow_charged_despite_pool_idx_set(self):
+        # Bug regression (match-COW crash): the scheduler samples fresh_cow
+        # BEFORE init_next_round_input; the match COW then sets mamba_pool_idx.
+        # Budgeting on the post-match pool_idx zeroed the charge for every
+        # queued request — the COW drained the hard free list unbudgeted and
+        # died on free=0. With fresh_cow=True the charge must apply even
+        # though pool_idx is already set (both warm=1 and cold=factor).
+        adder = self._adder(static=True)
+        # warm (boundary covered, no branching) with pool_idx set by the COW
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 64, None, has_pool_idx=True), fresh_cow=True), 1
+        )
+        # cold (branching) with pool_idx set by the COW
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._budget(adder, self._req(64, 100, 64, has_pool_idx=True), fresh_cow=True), 3
+        )
+
+    def test_feature_off_charges_cold_factor(self):
+        # Without --system-prompt every request is "cold" in slot terms (full
+        # ping-pong); the factor-3 charge matches alloc_req_slots' accounting.
+        adder = self._adder(static=True)
+        self.assertEqual(self._budget(adder, self._req(None, 0, None)), 3)
+
+    def test_match_headroom(self):
+        # Bug regression (match-COW crash, deep waiting queue): the scheduler
+        # must stop pulling new requests once the remaining slot budget is
+        # below a worst-case cold request, because init_next_round_input's
+        # mamba COW allocates BEFORE add_one_req can reject. Headroom = the
+        # cold factor on the static pool (lazy variant = 2), on the shared
+        # pool too, and 0 (pre-check disabled) without a mamba pool.
+        from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_policy import PrefillAdder
+
+        self.assertEqual(PrefillAdder._mamba_match_headroom(self._adder(static=True)), 3)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            PrefillAdder._mamba_match_headroom(self._adder(static=True, lazy=True)), 2
+        )
+        no_mamba = SimpleNamespace(
+            _mamba_slot_cost=0, _static_mamba_slots=False, tree_cache=None
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(PrefillAdder._mamba_match_headroom(no_mamba), 0)
+        shared = SimpleNamespace(
+            _mamba_slot_cost=64,
+            _static_mamba_slots=False,
+            tree_cache=self._adder(static=True).tree_cache,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(PrefillAdder._mamba_match_headroom(shared), 3)
+
+
+class _FakeArgs:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        system_prompt,
+        model_path="/tmp/model",
+        tokenizer_path=None,
+        trust_remote_code=True,
+        mamba_cache_chunk_size=64,
+    ):
+        self.system_prompt = system_prompt
+        self.model_path = model_path
+        self.tokenizer_path = tokenizer_path
+        self.trust_remote_code = trust_remote_code
+        self.mamba_cache_chunk_size = mamba_cache_chunk_size
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

## Update: production-verified fix chain added

The new commits (49e54ff289..93356ed393) are a chain of fixes for issues found when this feature ran in a production deployment (internally, on the v0.5.17-based release). They are backported onto this branch with adaptations to current main (the internal branch predates the `ReqKvInfo` migration and the removal of the `MAMBA_STATE_PER_REQ_*` constants). Summary, in causal order:

**1. Unaligned boundary crash (49e54ff289)** — the original padding-up alignment altered the token stream and a boundary that fails the identity probe at request time left the mamba pool sized for the warm steady state while every request stayed cold (over-admission crash). Now:
- The shared prefix is truncated **down** to the chunk grid instead of padded up — the full token stream stays byte-identical to the native render (the removed tail is re-prefilled per request, giving up only its cache reuse).
- A startup probe (`probe_system_prefix_or_disable`) runs **before any subprocess forks**: on probe failure the flag is cleared so pool sizing and runtime behavior stay consistent (feature-off everywhere).
- A slot-count admission budget is added for the static (non-shared) hybrid mamba pool.

**2. Phantom evictable credit (80e25e3750)** — the static-pool budget counted `mamba_evictable_size()`, but the match-time COW can only draw from the hard free list (its evict-retry can be blocked by locks on the shared boundary node). Now hard free slots only.

**3. Waiting-queue throttle (6a6f6ffacc + e29f58503d)** — the match-time mamba COW allocates the request's running slot *before* `add_one_req` can reject it, so a deep waiting queue drained the hard free list and died on free=0. The scheduler now stops pulling new requests once the remaining slot budget can't cover a worst-case cold request (`_mamba_match_headroom`).

**4. Audit logs (a08d87f9e0 + 092a49ec50)** — periodic `[MambaAudit]` lines reconcile the physical pool state against logical holders; made slot leaks and the crash root cause observable.

**5. Budget blind to match-time COW (1bf88bde57)** — the slot budget keyed on `mamba_pool_idx is None`, but the match COW sets that field *before* the budget runs, so every queued request was charged zero while its COW drained the free list. Fixed by sampling `fresh_cow` pre-match. Also: the warm sentinel ping-pong buffer is guarded against decode post-processing (it would otherwise free reserved slot 0 into the allocator), the token-concat fast path only engages when the leading system message content equals the fixed prompt (a client-supplied different system must not be silently replaced), and a per-request render failure now falls back to the full render instead of raising.

Unit tests grew from 29 to 44 cases covering the truncate-down invariants, the startup probe gate, the static-pool budget, the match headroom, and the fresh_cow accounting.
